answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared registry, the atlas of verified agents, before it can transact. Newcomers start on a low terrace with capped volume, and only rise as their stake ages and their behaviour stays honest. The delta between a sybil's cost and its gain then turns negative: spawning a hundred fake agents means locking a hundred stakes and waiting through the same probation, while a single misbehaving identity loses its bond. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay per identity, forever.
